warn-amber-dark.purpose: Maintenance badge, warning log lines, needs-attention icons.

danger-red-dark.purpose: Destructive buttons, failures, errors, disconnected state.

surface-raised-dark.purpose: Dialogs, palette, popovers, toasts, save bar.

sunken-dark.purpose: Segmented tracks, selected nav, pills, jobs, footers; also light hover.

hover-dark.purpose: Hover tint on nav, rows, quiet buttons.

line-strong-dark.purpose: Control borders, scrollbar thumb, switch track.

text-dark.purpose: Primary copy; inverted primary button fill.

narrative.overview:
rconsole is the room an operator walks into to check on one server and leave again. Everything resident on screen is neutral: near-white or near-black surfaces, hairline borders, grey text in three steps. Colour is spent only where it says something, either the single violet accent (focus, links, switches, charts, unsaved state) or a status hue (ok, warning, danger). The result reads like a Vercel-class enterprise console and sits beside winterstetter.io as the same family: Inter, JetBrains Mono, the same violet, the same hairline neutrals.

Density is moderate: 34px controls, 14px body, 20px panel padding, 28px page gutters. Hierarchy comes from weight (500/600) and the three text greys, not from size jumps or colour fields. Light and dark follow `prefers-color-scheme`; dark is not an inversion but its own neutral ramp with the accent and status hues lifted for contrast.

The previous "identity program" world (per-area colours, coloured title fields, 4px bands, 2px corners, uppercase condensed labels) is retired. Its variable names survive only as aliases (see Colors).
keyCharacteristics: Neutral surfaces with 1px hairlines; no colour fields.
One violet accent, used sparingly; primary actions are the inverted neutral.
Status colour keeps meaning: green ok, amber warning, red danger.
Inter for UI, JetBrains Mono for machine text; sentence-case labels; tabular numerals.
Flat at rest; shadows only on things that float.

rules.name: The One Violet Rule
rules.body: Violet marks focus, links, live data and unsaved or pending state. It never fills a button or a panel; if a screen shows more than a few violet marks at rest, one is wrong.

rules.name: The Inverted Primary Rule
rules.body: The primary action is the text colour as fill with the page colour as text (near-black on light, near-white on dark). Emphasis comes from contrast, not hue.

rules.name: The Status Keeps Meaning Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red appear only for ok, warning and danger. Red is never decorative; tinted status surfaces mix 5-14% of the hue into the surface with a 30-45% hue border.

rules.name: The Quiet Health Rule
rules.body: Health readouts are neutral text when nominal; "needs attention" adds an amber pictogram, "critical" turns the value red.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are 12px, weight 500, text-3, sentence case, no letter-spacing. The stylesheet carries no `text-transform`.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change (readouts, counts, tables, charts, versions, countdown) uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Machine Text Rule
rules.body: Anything typed to or emitted by the server is JetBrains Mono; anything written for a person is Inter.

rules.name: The Only Overlays Float Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to dialogs, the palette, popovers, tooltips, toasts and the sticky save bar. Anything resident in the layout is flat, with at most the light hairline.

rules.name: The Three Radii Rule
rules.body: 6px for things you operate, 10px for things that contain, 12px for things that float above. Round shapes only for pills, dots and switches.

dos: Do build every resident surface from page, surface and sunken with 1px line borders.
Do use the inverted neutral for the one primary action in a panel, and the default bordered button for the rest.
Do reserve violet for focus, links, live data and unsaved or pending state (The One Violet Rule).
Do keep status hues to their meaning and tint status surfaces lightly (5-14% fill, 30-45% border).
Do write labels in sentence case at 12px weight 500 in text-3, and use tabular numerals for changing numbers.
Do set machine text (log, prompt, keys, versions) in JetBrains Mono.
Do use 6px for controls, 10px for containers, 12px for overlays.
Do design both themes; check dark values against the dark ramp, not by inverting light.
donts: Don't fill buttons, panels or headers with the accent or any status hue except a confirming danger button.
Don't reintroduce per-area colours, coloured title fields, bands or 2px corners from the retired identity program.
Don't use uppercase, letter-spaced labels or kickers above headings.
Don't put shadows on resident layout beyond the light hairline.
Don't use red for anything that is not a danger or failure.
Don't reference the legacy `--c-*` or `--area` aliases in new code; use `--accent`, `--ok`, `--warn`, `--c-danger`.
